newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: GD Express revamps road network.
newsitem.headline: GD Express revamps road network.

text.p: GD Express Worldwide, the express mail company, has completed a programme geared to improve the performance of its road haulage throughout Europe, a company statement said.
GD Express, which trades as TNT Express Worldwide, headquatered in Amsterdam, said it had completed an in-house programme known as the "European road network rationalisation project".
The company now aims to create five Freight Management Centres in Northampton, Paris, Troisdorf in Germany, Stockholm and Arnhem in the Netherlands.

GD Express said the centres will co-ordinate regional operations and monitor and control all road movements across the European continent, which will lead to improved communications for road haulage operators and customers.

A new information technology system is being installed at all of the centres to provide real-time information to improve the management of TNT's weekly 4,500-plus linehaul road movements between the company's 135 hubs and depots throughout Europe.
GD Express is jointly owned by TNT Ltd, the Australian transport group and GD Net BV, a partnership of the Postal Adminstrations of the Netherlands and Sweden.
